henry.title: The Three Sisters: Ancient Farming in New Mexico
henry.intro: Long ago, Ancestral Puebloan farmers grew corn, beans, and squash together, called the Three Sisters. Corn holds up the beans, and squash leaves shade the soil.
steps: Look at the Bandelier National Monument page (cliff homes of farming families).
worksheet: How does each sister help the others?
Why was water so important for farmers in New Mexico's desert?
Name one food you eat that comes from corn.
Draw a Three Sisters garden and label each plant.
links: Look at the photos of cliff homes where farming families lived.

frankie.title: Long-Ago Farmers
frankie.intro: Long ago, families in New Mexico grew corn, beans, and squash. They worked together like a team!
steps: Look at Bandelier pictures with a grown-up.
Draw a garden on your worksheet.
links: Look at the pictures with a grown-up. Find the cliff homes!
